title: Feelings & opinions
verifiedBy: Claude Fable 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: porque gives the REASON and por eso gives the CONSEQUENCE. They take the same two facts and put them in opposite orders: No quiero café porque estoy cansado — the tiredness explains the refusal. Estoy cansado, por eso no quiero café — the tiredness comes first and the refusal follows from it.

Three spellings, three different words, and they sound almost the same out loud: ¿Por qué…? is "why" — two words with an accent. porque is "because" — one word, no accent. por eso is "so" — two words, no accent. The writing is where the difference lives, which is why getting it wrong is an orthography problem and not a grammar one.

Feelings ride estar + an adjective, and the adjective agrees with the SUBJECT — whoever the sentence is about, not whoever is speaking. Estoy cansado is a man about himself; Estoy cansada is a woman about herself; ¿Estás cansada? is asked OF a woman, whoever is asking.

M2's split, back for the last time in this level: how someone feels is estar (Estoy triste, Estoy enfermo), and what something IS stays ser (El café es fuerte). Neither is about permanence — a feeling is a state, and strong coffee is a kind of coffee.

An adjective ending in -e has one shape for both genders — triste, fuerte, M3's caliente — and only changes for number: tristes, fuertes. Only the -o/-a kind splits, and mal is not an adjective at all, so it never moves either.

por eso joins two complete sentences, so something has to separate them: a comma, or a full stop. Estoy cansado, por eso no quiero café. porque needs nothing in front of it, because the piece it introduces is not a complete sentence on its own.

A ¿por qué? question keeps the order of the statement behind it, exactly as every question in this course has: ¿Por qué no quieres café? Nothing is inverted, no word for "do" appears, and the answer usually comes back with porque.

por is not being taught here as a word. It lives inside three fixed phrases you already have — por la mañana (M4), por favor (M8) — and now inside por qué and por eso. Spanish does have a por / para contrast, and no sentence in this level needs it, so do not try to translate the por on its own.

gustar keeps its reversal even when an opinion is attached: Me gusta el café porque es fuerte. The coffee is the thing that pleases AND the thing that is strong — both halves of the sentence agree with it, and neither agrees with you.
bien and mal answer "how are you" and never change for gender: Estoy bien · Estoy mal. They are the two words in this module that a woman and a man say identically.

words.note: Today — the third of the set with M5's ayer and M6's mañana. Like them it usually opens the sentence and leaves the verb alone.
Tired, and the ending belongs to whoever the sentence is about: cansado for a man, cansada for a woman, cansados / cansadas for more than one. Being tired is a state, so it always arrives with estar.

sentences.trap: estoy, not soy. A feeling is a state you are in — soy cansado would be claiming that being tired is the kind of person you are.
sentences.sound: can-SA-do. The stress is in the middle, and the d near the end is soft, closer to the th of English "the".

variations.display: Hoy estoy cansada
variations.cue: Today I'm tired (a woman speaking)
variations.changed: -o → -a: the ending follows the subject

variations.display: Hoy estoy bien
variations.cue: Today I'm well
variations.changed: M2's bien, which never changes for anyone

variations.display: Ana está cansada hoy
variations.cue: Ana is tired today
variations.changed: está for her — and cansada agrees with Ana, not with you

mistake.why: Feelings take estar: Hoy estoy cansado.

sentences.mnemonic: Feelings are states, and states are estar.

sentences.display: No quiero café porque estoy cansado
sentences.cue: I don't want coffee because I'm tired
sentences.literal: Not I-want coffee because I-am tired(m)

words.note: One word, no accent, and it introduces the reason. What follows it is a whole sentence with its own verb: porque estoy cansado. Its two-word, accented cousin ¿por qué? is the question, not the answer.

sentences.trap: porque and por qué sound alike and are not interchangeable. If it can be answered, it is ¿por qué?; if it is doing the answering, it is porque.
sentences.sound: por-QUE, stressed on the second syllable, with the qu as a plain k. Said aloud it is nearly the same noise as por qué — only the sentence tells them apart.

variations.display: No quiero café porque estoy enfermo
variations.cue: I don't want coffee because I'm ill
variations.changed: swap the reason

variations.display: No voy a trabajar porque estoy cansado
variations.cue: I'm not going to work because I'm tired
variations.changed: M6's plan as the thing being explained

variations.display: No quiero comer porque comí mucho
variations.cue: I don't want to eat because I ate a lot
variations.changed: the reason can sit in the past — M5's comí

mistake.display: No quiero café por que estoy cansado
mistake.why: "Because" is one word with no accent: porque.

sentences.usage: Refusing something and softening it with a reason.
sentences.mnemonic: One word, no accent, gives the reason.

sentences.display: Estoy cansado, por eso no quiero café
sentences.cue: I'm tired, so I don't want coffee
sentences.literal: I-am tired(m), for that not I-want coffee

words.note: Literally "for that", and it introduces the CONSEQUENCE — the opposite end of the pair from porque. It joins two complete sentences, so it wants a comma or a full stop in front of it.

sentences.trap: This is S02 turned around. Same tiredness, same refusal, opposite order: porque puts the reason second, por eso puts it first. Choosing between them is choosing which half you want to lead with.
sentences.sound: por-E-so, the three syllables running together, and the r is one light tap.

variations.display: Estoy cansada, por eso no quiero café
variations.cue: I'm tired, so I don't want coffee (a woman speaking)
variations.changed: the adjective follows the subject; por eso does not move

variations.display: Estoy cansado, por eso voy a comer temprano
variations.cue: I'm tired, so I'm going to eat early
variations.changed: another consequence

variations.display: Estoy cansado, por eso necesito café
variations.cue: I'm tired, so I need coffee
variations.changed: the same state argues the other way — necesito, not no quiero

mistake.display: Estoy cansado por eso no quiero café
mistake.why: Two full sentences need a break between them: Estoy cansado, por eso no quiero café.

sentences.mnemonic: porque looks back at the reason; por eso looks forward to the result.

words.note: Two words with an accent on the second — the question. Built out of por and M4's qué, and a different thing from the one-word porque that answers it. Space and accent keep them apart.

sentences.trap: English inserts "do" to ask this — "why DO you not want" — and Spanish inserts nothing. The statement no quieres café keeps its order and por qué goes on the front.
sentences.sound: por QUÉ: two words, the stress on the second, and a tiny gap between them that porque does not have.

variations.display: ¿Por qué estás cansada?
variations.cue: Why are you tired? (asked of a woman)
variations.changed: the -a agrees with the person being asked

variations.display: ¿Por qué no vas a trabajar?
variations.cue: Why aren't you going to work?
variations.changed: M6's plan, questioned

variations.display: Porque estoy enfermo
variations.cue: Because I'm ill
variations.changed: the answer — porque and the reason, with nothing in front of it

mistake.why: The question is two words and takes the accent: ¿Por qué no quieres café?

sentences.mnemonic: Two words ask, one word answers.

sentences.display: Estoy contento porque mañana no trabajo
sentences.cue: I'm happy because tomorrow I don't work
sentences.literal: I-am happy(m) because tomorrow not I-work

words.note: Happy in the sense of pleased about something, which is why it goes with estar and agrees with the subject: contento / contenta. feliz is the deeper, longer-lasting kind and takes either verb.

sentences.trap: The reason can be about tomorrow while the feeling is about now — porque does not care what tense follows it. Here M6's present-as-future does the second half.
sentences.sound: con-TEN-to, stress in the middle, and both o's are short and pure.

variations.display: Estoy contenta porque mañana no trabajo
variations.cue: I'm happy because tomorrow I don't work (a woman speaking)
variations.changed: -o → -a for the subject

variations.display: Estoy contento porque hoy no trabajo
variations.cue: I'm happy because today I don't work
variations.changed: the reason moves to today

variations.display: ¿Por qué estás contento?
variations.cue: Why are you happy? (asked of a man)
variations.changed: the question that fishes for the reason — and -o for the man asked

mistake.display: Soy contento porque mañana no trabajo
mistake.why: Being pleased is a state: Estoy contento.

sentences.usage: Saying why the day is going well.
sentences.mnemonic: contento is pleased-right-now, so it is estar's.

words.note: Sad — and an -e adjective, so it has one shape for a man and a woman alike, exactly like M3's caliente. It only moves for number: estamos tristes.

sentences.trap: Nothing to agree here. Learners who have just met cansado / cansada reach for *trista, which does not exist — the -e adjectives sit out the gender game entirely.
sentences.sound: TRIS-te. The tr is crisp and the r is a single tap; the final e is short, never an English "ay".

variations.display: ¿Por qué estás cansado?
variations.cue: Why are you tired? (asked of a man)
variations.changed: an -o/-a adjective, so this one does agree

variations.display: Estoy triste porque mañana trabajo
variations.cue: I'm sad because tomorrow I work
variations.changed: the answer, with its reason

variations.display: ¿Por qué está usted triste?
variations.cue: Why are you sad? (polite)
variations.changed: usted takes está — the same concern, in the polite register

mistake.why: triste has no feminine form: ¿Por qué estás triste?

sentences.display: Estoy enfermo, por eso no voy a trabajar
sentences.cue: I'm ill, so I'm not going to work
sentences.literal: I-am ill(m), for that not I-go to to-work

words.note: Ill, agreeing with the subject: enfermo / enferma. estar enfermo is being ill just now; ser enfermo is not how Spanish talks about people at all — the illness is a state, never an identity.

sentences.trap: Both halves need their own negative-free reading: estoy enfermo is the fact, no voy a trabajar is what follows from it, and the no belongs to the going — M6's rule, unchanged.
sentences.sound: en-FER-mo. The r is one tap and the first syllable is nasal, close to English "en".

variations.display: Estoy enferma, por eso no voy a trabajar
variations.cue: I'm ill, so I'm not going to work (a woman speaking)
variations.changed: -o → -a for the subject

variations.display: No voy a trabajar porque estoy enfermo
variations.cue: I'm not going to work because I'm ill
variations.changed: the same two facts with porque, in the other order

variations.display: Hoy estoy enfermo, por eso no trabajo
variations.cue: Today I'm ill, so I'm not working
variations.changed: hoy pins it to today, and the plain present does the rest

mistake.display: Soy enfermo, por eso no voy a trabajar
mistake.why: Being ill is a state: Estoy enfermo.

sentences.mnemonic: estar enfermo today; nobody is ser enfermo.

sentences.display: Me gusta el café porque es fuerte
sentences.cue: I like coffee because it's strong
sentences.literal: To-me pleases the coffee because it-is strong

words.note: Strong — of coffee, of a person, of a smell. Another -e adjective, so one shape for both genders: un café fuerte, una sopa fuerte.

sentences.trap: Two agreements in one sentence and neither of them is with you: gusta agrees with el café, and es agrees with el café. You appear only as the me at the front.
sentences.sound: FUER-te, one glide in the middle — fwer, not fu-er — and the stress on it.

variations.display: No me gusta el café porque es fuerte
variations.cue: I don't like coffee because it's strong
variations.changed: the same reason, the opposite opinion

variations.display: Me gusta la sopa porque está caliente
variations.cue: I like the soup because it's hot
variations.changed: a temperature right now, so estar rather than ser

variations.display: Me gustan las sopas porque están calientes
variations.cue: I like the soups because they're hot
variations.changed: the whole line pivots plural — gustan, las sopas, están, calientes

mistake.display: Me gusto el café porque es fuerte
mistake.why: gusto would mean you are the thing doing the pleasing. The coffee pleases: me gusta el café.

sentences.usage: An opinion with a reason attached — the whole job of this module.
sentences.mnemonic: The coffee pleases and the coffee is strong. You are just the me.

sentences.display: Estoy mal, por eso no estudio
sentences.cue: I'm not well, so I'm not studying
sentences.literal: I-am badly, for that not I-study

words.note: The opposite of M2's bien, and like bien it is an adverb: it never changes for gender or number. The adjective "bad" is malo / mala, and it is a different word for a different job.

sentences.trap: Estoy mal is how you are, not what you are. It says the day is going badly, or that you feel unwell — it never means "I am a bad person".
sentences.sound: One syllable, MAL, with a light l — Spanish has no dark English "l" at the end of a word.

variations.display: Estoy mal porque no comí
variations.cue: I'm not well because I didn't eat
variations.changed: M5's preterite as the reason

variations.display: Estoy bien, por eso voy a estudiar
variations.cue: I'm well, so I'm going to study
variations.changed: the opposite state, the opposite consequence

variations.display: Ana está mal hoy
variations.cue: Ana is unwell today
variations.changed: mal for her too — it never agrees with anyone

mistake.display: Estoy mala, por eso no estudio
mistake.why: mal has no feminine — it is an adverb. Estoy mala exists but says you are ill, not that things are going badly.

sentences.usage: Saying you are having a bad day without going into detail.
sentences.mnemonic: bien and mal: how, not what — so they never change.

sentences.cue: I'm nervous because tomorrow I work

words.note: Nervous, agreeing with the subject — nerviosa here because the subject is a woman, nervioso when he is a man. The row is headed by the shape this sentence shows; all four are one word.

sentences.trap: The -a belongs to the subject and not to the speaker. Say this to a man and it becomes ¿Estás nervioso?; say it about yourself and it follows you. It is the same law M3's roja followed for the apple.
sentences.sound: ner-VIO-sa. The v is soft, somewhere between an English b and v, and the io is one glide.

variations.display: Estoy nervioso porque mañana trabajo
variations.cue: I'm nervous because tomorrow I work (a man speaking)
variations.changed: -a → -o for the subject

variations.display: ¿Estás nerviosa?
variations.cue: Are you nervous? (asked of a woman)
variations.changed: now the ending follows the person being asked

variations.display: Mañana trabajo, por eso estoy nerviosa
variations.cue: Tomorrow I work, so I'm nervous
variations.changed: the same two facts welded the other way — the reason first, por eso in the middle

mistake.why: Being nervous about tomorrow is a state: Estoy nerviosa. Soy nerviosa would say it is your character.

sentences.usage: Naming the feeling and its cause in one breath.
sentences.mnemonic: The ending follows the subject — ask who the sentence is about.
